# Zelta Design, full site content

> Zelta Design is a full-service architecture firm in Nutley, New Jersey, specializing in restaurant and commercial projects. The firm has completed over 1,000 projects for +40 brands and is licensed in 25 states. It handles a project end to end: site survey, schematic design, construction documents, permitting and plan review, code and accessibility compliance, MEP coordination and construction administration.
> Generated from the site's own data. Every project below links to its page.

- Sector focus: quick-service restaurants, fast casual, cafes, and commercial tenant fit-outs

## Projects

### Dave's Hot Chicken - White Plains, NY

Dave's Hot Chicken in White Plains, New York was designed by Zelta Design. Full-height murals, graffiti artwork and neon signage define the dining room. Red exposed ductwork and metal chairs accompany concrete floors and wood wainscoting.

Address: 489 Tarrytown Road, White Plains, NY 10607. Floor area: 4,060 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-white-plains/

### Dave's Hot Chicken - Sumter, SC

Dave's Hot Chicken in Sumter, South Carolina was designed by Zelta Design. Freestanding and set back from the road with its own parking field, this Dave's Hot Chicken in Sumter includes a drive-thru lane and a covered patio. Wood-toned paneling and red trim wrap the exterior between full-height murals, while the dining room pairs the same murals with exposed red ductwork and wood tabletops. A separate pickup shelf by the side door keeps mobile orders apart from the counter. The layout separates dine-in, walk-up pickup and drive-thru orders, so three types of customers move through without crossing paths.

Address: 1135 Broad St., Sumter, SC 29150. Floor area: 3,110 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-sumter/

### Dave's Hot Chicken - Greenville, NC

Dave's Hot Chicken in Greenville, North Carolina was designed by Zelta Design. Red shade sails cover the patio at this Dave's Hot Chicken, a freestanding building in the Greenville Plaza shopping center. A large graphic mural wraps the entry tower above the door, continuing across interior walls and the ceiling inside. Red tables and chairs fill both the patio and dining room, and a service opening connects the ordering counter directly to the kitchen. The layout keeps entry, ordering and pickup in a single sequence, moving takeaway customers through quickly while patio diners stay clear of the line.

Address: 114 Red Banks Road, Greenville, NC 27858. Floor area: 2,207 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-greenville/

### PopUp Bagels - Winter Park, FL

PopUp Bagels in Winter Park, Florida was designed by Zelta Design. PopUp Bagels' Winter Park shop occupies a freestanding building on South Orlando Avenue, wrapped in white stucco with a corner glass storefront. A black-and-white checkerboard floor and black ceiling set off a photo-collage wall of customers near the register, with a disco ball and a director's chair marking a small waiting nook by the window. Yellow stools line the sidewalk outside for grab-and-go customers, keeping the 953-square-foot interior focused on ordering, pickup, and retail rather than seating.

Address: 646 South Orlando Avenue, Winter Park, FL 32789. Floor area: 953 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/popup-bagels-winter-park/

### PopUp Bagels - Rockledge, FL

PopUp Bagels in Rockledge, Florida was designed by Zelta Design. At 2105 Viera Boulevard in Rockledge, PopUp Bagels takes an inline bay next to Cava beneath a black awning and gray lap siding. The 1,167-square-foot interior repeats the brand's black-and-white checkerboard floor and photo-collage wall, this time alongside a ribbed black counter with a glowing script logo, white subway tile behind the kitchen pass, and a chalkboard menu listing bagels and schmears. Yellow stools out front give walk-up customers somewhere to wait.

Address: 2105 Viera Boulevard, Rockledge, FL 32955. Floor area: 1,167 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/popup-bagels-viera/

### Dunkin' - World Trade Center, NY

Dunkin' in World Trade Center, New York was designed by Zelta Design. Inside the Oculus at the World Trade Center transit hub, this Dunkin' sits on a curved corner storefront between the concourse's stone columns, steps from retail traffic. The plan is a compact kiosk with no seating, built for pass-through commuters. We used a floor-to-ceiling curved glass front, warm wood-tone tile behind the counter, and an orange light band over the pastry case to keep the brand visible from both directions of the walkway. Customers can see the full donut case and order the moment they step off the escalator.

Address: 185 Greenwich Street LL2440, New York, NY 10006.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/dunkin-oculus-world-trade-center/

### Dunkin' - Lower Manhattan, NY

Dunkin' in Lower Manhattan, Manhattan, New York was designed by Zelta Design. Set into a brick building on lower Broadway, this Dunkin' takes a narrow storefront bay between neighboring retail, with a single white sign band above the entrance. The tight footprint runs coffee and pastry service without a dining area, built around foot traffic on the block. Inside, orange accent lighting and a wall graphic mark the borough by name over a straightforward wood-tone counter. It is built for the walk-up order and go, not a sit-down stop.

Address: 336 Broadway, New York, NY.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/dunkin-336-broadway/

### Dave's Hot Chicken - Bedford-Stuyvesant, NY

Dave's Hot Chicken in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, New York was designed by Zelta Design. This Dave's Hot Chicken occupies a ground-floor storefront in a red-brick walk-up on Fulton Street in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, between a pizzeria and a shuttered retail bay. A swirling multicolor mural covers the black storefront glass and doorway, giving the narrow entrance a bold identity against the older facade. Inside, red stool seating sits near exposed red ductwork threading across the ceiling, keeping the small dining area close to the order counter for fast pickup on a busy commercial block.

Address: 1192 Fulton Street, Brooklyn, NY 11216.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-1192-fulton-street/

### Dave's Hot Chicken - Florence, SC

Dave's Hot Chicken in Florence, South Carolina was designed by Zelta Design. Set at a corner site along West Palmetto Street in Florence, this freestanding Dave's Hot Chicken has its own parking and a covered patio wrapping the building. A continuous red neon band traces the roofline above graphic murals, while glass storefronts wrap two sides of the dining room so red patio seating is visible from the road at night. Inside, exposed red ductwork and a wraparound counter keep ordering and pickup compact, so the drive-by visibility and quick service work together for a shopping-center location.

Address: 1923 West Palmetto Street, Florence, SC 29501.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-florence/

### Dave's Hot Chicken - Shelby, NC

Dave's Hot Chicken in Shelby, North Carolina was designed by Zelta Design. A new freestanding Dave's Hot Chicken on East Dixon Boulevard in Shelby, with a drive-thru lane and its own parking. The white building looks broken open by bright murals: panels of color burst through painted cracks, and on the side wall a classical bust in sunglasses takes a selfie. At night a red neon sign and roofline glow over the front windows. Inside, red ductwork runs beneath a painted sky ceiling, graffiti spells SHELBY across the dining room, and butcher-block tables with red metal chairs sit between a "Welcome to Dave's" marquee at the door and a counter with ordering kiosks.

Address: 1245 East Dixon Boulevard, Shelby, NC 28152.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/daves-hot-chicken-shelby/

### Chopsticks Charm Noodle Bar - Edison, NJ

Chopsticks Charm Noodle Bar in Edison, New Jersey was designed by Zelta Design. On Amboy Avenue in Edison, Chopsticks Charm Noodle Bar fills a storefront wrapped floor to ceiling in black-and-white line drawings of city streets and trees. A sculptural white tree rises through the center of a round communal table ringed by matching monochrome chairs, with faceted maneki-neko cat figures perched along a mirrored shelf near the open kitchen pass. The hand-drawn mural and sculptural centerpiece turn a single dining room into a destination rather than a simple counter stop.

Address: 1199 Amboy Avenue, Edison, NJ.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/chopsticks-charm-edison/

### Office Fit-Out - Midtown, NY

Office Fit-Out in Midtown, Manhattan, New York was designed by Zelta Design. On East 45th Street in Midtown Manhattan, this office fit-out turns a mid-rise floor into private offices and open desking behind glass partition walls. Exposed brick walls and ductwork stay visible throughout, paired with black leather club chairs, glass-top desks, and framed black-and-white city photography that plays off the exposed masonry. Felt privacy screens divide the open desking area from the glass-fronted offices, giving the real estate company a mix of private meeting space and collaborative desks within the same floor.

Address: 9 East 45th Street, New York, NY.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/office-9-east-45th-street/

Taco Bell occupies a storefront bay in a Schuyler Avenue shopping plaza in North Arlington, between neighboring retail tenants under a shared green awning. Inside, a dedicated late-night pickup window sits beside the entry, with a self-order kiosk and a separate mobile and delivery pickup shelf near the counter. A booth with a colorful abstract print sits along the front window for the customer dining room. Keeping order kiosks, counter service and pickup as separate stations lets the 1,548-square-foot space handle counter, mobile and late-night orders at once.

Address: 15 Schuyler Ave, North Arlington, NJ 07031. Floor area: 1,548 sq ft.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/taco-bell-15-schuyler-avenue/

### Dunkin’/Baskin Robbins - Bronx, NY

Dunkin' in Bronx, New York was designed by Zelta Design. This Mount Eden location combines Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins with a drive-thru, on a corner site built for both car and walk-in traffic. Inside, a curved donut case sits near the entry with the order counter and a self-service kiosk set back near the dining area, so mobile pickup and in-person ordering don't collide. Cream tile, wood-look counters, and a Baskin-Robbins freezer wall carry both brands' colors without clashing. The layout lets drive-thru, counter service, and seated guests all move through without crossing paths.

Address: 1733 Jerome Avenue, Bronx, NY 10453. Scope: drive-thru, multi-brand combo.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/dunkin-baskin-robbins-1733-jerome-avenue/

### Popeyes - Times Square, NY

Popeyes in Times Square, New York was designed by Zelta Design. Located in the heart of Times Square, this Popeyes flagship location has many unique elements. The building's exterior features a modern and sleek design with a large glass façade that would allow passersby to see inside. When arriving to the second floor (either by stairs or an elevator) guests are greeted by a spacious and open floor plan with ample seating options. The restaurant features a mix of booths and tables, as well as a bar-style seating area. To ensure efficient service, the restaurant has a state-of-the-art food transporter system that seamlessly transports food from the kitchen to the second floor seating area of the restaurant. The building is designed to maximize efficiency and customer satisfaction while also offering a visually stunning dining experience that will leave a lasting impression on guests.

Address: 1530 Broadway, New York, NY 10036. Program: flagship.

Source: https://www.zeltadesign.com/project/popeyes/
